title: What are indexes in SQL Server and how do they improve performance?
description: Learn about clustered, non-clustered, and covering indexes.

data.text: **Question:** What are indexes in SQL Server and how do they improve performance?

Indexes are database objects that improve query performance by allowing SQL Server to find data quickly. They work like a book index - instead of scanning the entire table, SQL Server can jump directly to the relevant rows.

**Clustered Index:**
- Determines the physical order of data in the table
- A table can have only one clustered index
- The data is stored at the leaf level
- Primary key usually creates a clustered index

**Non-Clustered Index:**
- Separate structure from the data rows
- Contains index key values and pointers to data
- A table can have multiple non-clustered indexes
- Stored as B-tree structure

**Covering Index:**
- Includes all columns needed by a query
- Eliminates need to look up the base table
- Significantly improves query performance

data.title: Indexes
data.code:
-- Create a non-clustered index
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Employees_LastName
ON Employees (LastName);

-- Covering index
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Orders_Covering
ON Orders (CustomerID)
INCLUDE (OrderDate, TotalAmount);

-- Query using the index
SELECT CustomerID, OrderDate, TotalAmount
FROM Orders
WHERE CustomerID = 123;

data.text: Interviewers want to assess understanding of index types, when to use each, and how indexes affect query performance.

items: What is an index scan vs index seek?

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Use indexes strategically - they speed up reads but can slow down writes.
